thread:
emma: Quick follow-up from the runtime section in today's all-hands. I want a short live thread for the three asks we had: batching thresholds, KV cache prioritization, and kernel rollout schedule. Keeping this tight.
raja: thanks emma Two quick clarifications: when we say "adaptive batching" in the roadmap, do we mean dynamic microbatch size per-worker or cross-worker pooling first?
ben: ops preference: start with per-worker adaptive microbatching (simpler), then evaluate cross-worker pooling after we have telemetry. Cross-worker pooling has more lock/coord complexity.
claire: product note customers care about predictable latency. If we do per-worker, we need clear p95 bounds and a way to pin request priority to bypass batching.
emma: agreed. Proposal: default adaptive microbatch with a configurable max_batch_size and a client-side priority header to opt out. Example config snippet we discussed:
```
batching:
  mode: adaptive
  max_batch_size: 64
  target_latency_ms: 50
  priority_header: X-Request-Priority
```
raja: that config looks good. For target_latency_ms, should that be soft or enforced? My vote: soft target, with SLA customers able to enforce hard latency routes (priority bypass).
maria: ops action run a small experiment next week: enable adaptive microbatching on a couple of dev clusters with max_batch_size 32/64 and measure p50/p95 for short (16/32) and long (512) seq-lens. Report by Friday.
ben: on KV cache prioritization we currently TTL prefixes for 5m. Roadmap idea was to add a hot-prefix scoring that uses request frequency and recency. We should also cap memory by weight so one tenant doesn't evict everyone.
lila: (note: not in participants list, but ops-bot will include) ops-bot: reminder: tenant isolation policies require per-tenant cache budget; default is 5% of node mem.
claire: product asks can we expose cache-hit metrics per-route in the console? This will help customers understand when to increase cache budgets.
raja: yes, expose route-level cache_hit_rate and median_prefix_ttl. Also add an alert when tenant cache eviction rate spikes > 3x baseline.
emma: kernel rollout question what is the timeframe for kernel-v4 staging vs full rollout? We heard "two-phase canary" in the talk but want dates.
ben: timeline update we complete kernel-v4 microbench suite on Monday. If no regressions, start stage-1 canary (10% traffic for non-SLA tiers) in 10 days. Stage-2 (50%) two weeks after that, then full by end of quarter if no blockers.
maria: telemetry requirement: every kernel canary must run model-determinism checks (sampled prompts), end-to-end quality evals, and token-level latency histograms. If any semantic drift > 0.8 BLEU-ish metric threshold on our eval set, auto-roll back.
raja: small ask please define the exact regression thresholds for the RFC. Right now "drift" is vague.
enmma: (typo correction) emma: +1. ben and maria, can you publish a short RFC with numerical thresholds by Wednesday?
ben: will do. Draft will include perf thresholds (p95 regression < 5% allowed), quality thresholds (eval-bucket delta < 1.0 on our internal metric), and memory limits.
claire: customer comms we should add a short note in the release notes template when kernels change: what changed, expected perf impact, and how customers can opt into conservative routes.
emma: good point. action items: 1) maria run microbatch experiment and share results (maria) 2) ben publish kernel-v4 RFC with thresholds (ben) 3) platform to add route-level cache metrics to backlog (raja/platform) 4) product to draft release-note snippet (claire). Ops-bot, attach meeting notes when available.
ops-bot: Meeting notes uploaded: https://redwood.internal/notes/allhands-2654321000. :white_check_mark:
emma: thanks all I'll follow up with a short RFC thread linking these action items. Ping me if you need help.
